record.original_question: Let R(u) be the relaxed energy for maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2), where Ω=B^3, deg g=0, and R is defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous S^2-valued maps with the same boundary trace g. Are minimizers of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(u):u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)} continuous on Ω̄? At least, is one minimizer continuous?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 ([2]). Are the minimizers of (4.9) continuous on Ω̄? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth boundary datum of topological degree zero. Consider the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e.}, \ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}.$$
For $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$, define the relaxed Dirichlet energy
$$R(u) = \inf\Big\{ \liminf_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u_n|^2\,dx : u_n \in C^0(\overline{\Omega}; S^2) \cap H^1(\Omega; S^2),\ u_n|_{\partial\Omega} = g,\ u_n \rightharpoonup u \text{ in } H^1 \Big\}.$$
Consider the minimization problem
$$\min\{ R(u) : u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \}.$$
(a) Is every minimizer of this problem continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$?
(b) If not, does there always exist at least one minimizer that is continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$?

artifact.status_search_result: The question of continuity of minimizers of the Bethuel–Brezis–Coron relaxed energy for $H^1_g(B^3;S^2)$ maps with degree-zero boundary data is listed as an open problem in Brezis's list of favorite open problems and is discussed in the literature on relaxed energies; no published resolution (either proving continuity of all/some minimizers or exhibiting a discontinuous one) was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Study of minimizers of the relaxed energy functional from balls into S^2.
